title: Agent writes must preserve human authority across re-records
context: The /capture grilling token mints human_confirmed provenance, proving human vetting preceded a decision. Three distinct code paths allowed subsequent agent writes to silently erase this authority: re-record stripped the human_confirmed tier, agent testimony locked slots against human captures (contradicting its own comment), and premises deletion removed the recorded basis for validity. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Agent writes inherit and preserve all human authority markers (provenance tier, slot identity protection, premise basis) regardless of token status. Only explicit human action (via /capture or review --reject) can downgrade a human-vouched decision. Implemented by: (1) resolving capture token before overwrite guard so authority rules depend on it; (2) excluding agent_recorded from slot locks (only human_confirmed blocks); (3) carrying incumbent premises across re-records to maintain fail-open guarantee.
consequences: Human authority vouched via /capture cannot be accidentally erased by subsequent agent refinement
Premises forming a decision's validity basis survive re-records, maintaining premise-decay escalation integrity
Supply chain of human authority is now immutable except through explicit downgrades
Agents refining decisions must understand they cannot strip signatures or premises even when improving content
alternatives_rejected: Allowing agents to rewrite provenance tiers on re-record — inverts the stamp's whole purpose (prevent agents CLAIMING authority, not erasing it)
Keeping agent_recorded in slot-lock guards — blocks human captures, contradicts the stamp's contract to never lock slots against later human authority
Omitting premises on re-record for simplicity — silently loses decision's recorded basis and breaks premise-decay escalations while authority stays intact
